Marie the be{{ls}}t part.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Contemplatiue or Religious life, better then the Actiue and {{ls}}ecular.}}Tvvo notable examples, one of the life Actiue, in Martha: the other of the life Contēplatiue, in Marie: repre{{ls}}enting vnto vs, that in holy Church there {{ls}}hould be alwaies {{ls}}ome to {{ls}}erue God in both the{{ls}}e {{ls}}eueral {{ls}}orts. The life contemplatiue is here preferred before the actiue. the Religious of both {{ls}}exes are of that more excellent {{ls}}tate. and therfore our Prote{{ls}}tants haue wholy abandoned them out of their common wealth, which the true Church neuer wanted. But to {{ls}}ay truth, they haue neither Martha nor Marie. our Lord geue them grace to {{ls}}ee their mi{{ls}}erie. If ours were not an{{ls}}werable to their profe{{ls}}{{ls}}ion, or were degenerated, why haue they no new ones? if our Churches Votaries vowed vnlawful things, Cha{{ls}}titie, Pouertie, Obedience, Pilgrimage: what other Votaries or lawful vowes haue they? For, to offer voluntarily by vow (be{{ls}}ides the keeping of Gods commaundements, wherevnto we are bound by precept and promi{{ls}}e in our Bapti{{ls}}me) our {{ls}}oules, bodies, goods, or any other acceptable thing to God, is an acte of {{ls}}oueraine wor{{ls}}hip belonging to God onely: and there was neuer true religion without {{ls}}uch vowes and Votaries. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Vovves and votaries.}}If there be none in their whole Church that profe{{ls}}{{ls}}e contemplation, or that vow any thing at al to God voluntarily, neither in their bodies nor in their goods: God and the world knovv they haue no Church nor religion at al.
